newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on cool weather concern.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on cool weather concern.

text.p: Concerns about cuts in U.S. soybean production amid a forecast for mostly cool weather in the U.S. Midwest boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
Signals the market was oversold during Monday's slide also boosted prices, they said, as did a rumor China was seeking 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for October/November shipment.
"It was overdone yesterday. They acted as if the crop was harvested and in the bin and the crop isn't even mature," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10 day outlook and USDA's weekly crop ratings led the rally.
The NWS called for normal to below normal temperatures in the Midwest September 22-26, while the crop needs warm weather.

"I'm looking for smaller than average seed size and reduced yields," said Gary Pepper, University of Illinois extension specialist. "The ability of the soybean to fill seed is reduced when it is chilled during the night to temperatures below 50 degrees (Farenheit)."
Soybeans closed 1/2 to three cents per bushel higher, with November up three at $7.96.
Traders also noted speculation about the extent of frost damage that occurred over the weekend in the U.S. crop.
"There are a lot of stories going around about the extent of frost damage and that's keeping things stirred up," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
The editor of the Brock Report Tuesday told Reuters the weekend frost may have destroyed 15 million to 35 million bushels of soybeans.
Although the weather jitters boosted prices, the market ended well below the day's highs on fund long liquidation tied to profit taking and on local selling, the traders said.
"Nearly everyone who wanted to be long is already long and they're taking profits," a trader said.
"They tried to rally it but the one key ingredient that was missing was volume," Lespinasse said.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold 5.5 million bushels of November and Refco Inc was a net seller of roughly two million November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 50,000, down from 62,120 Monday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Continental Grain bought 400 January $8.00 calls and sold 400 January $10.00 calls at 33-1/2 to 34, traders said. Continental also bought 200 January $8.00 puts and sold 200 January $10.00 calls at 34 cents while Cargill Investor Services bought 400 January $8.00 calls and sold 400 January $10.00 calls at 34 cents, the traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 17,000, down from 23,210 Monday.
